In March 2026 the Burning Glass Institute and the Schultz Family Foundation, working with the Harvard Business School Project on Managing the Future of Work, published the **Where You Work Matters** list. It observed 12 million American workers in 55,000 roles across 1,750 employers and graded each on the quality of the jobs it actually creates, using observed employee outcomes rather than anything companies said about themselves. **Philadelphia Insurance Companies (PHLY) was one of just 22 employers to earn platinum badges in all three categories: Early Career Jobs, Growth Jobs and Stability Jobs.** Fast Company compared a top spot on that list to a restaurant earning a Michelin star. PHLY is a[$5 billion gross-written-premium](https://www.phly.com/aboutphly) specialty property/casualty carrier with 2,100 employees, an A++ (Superior) AM Best rating held since 2011, an A+ from S&P, a 92.6% combined ratio, and 120 niche market specialties, and it has been a member of the Tokio Marine Group since 2008. For a student, the unusual thing is not the size. It is that an independent study of what actually happens to entry-level workers put this company in the American top 22.

## What Is a Philadelphia Insurance Companies Internship?


A Philadelphia Insurance Companies internship is PHLY’s exclusive Summer Associates Program: a paid, 10-week placement (June through August) that embeds college students into one of seven departments at a $5 billion specialty property/casualty carrier rated A++ by AM Best. The programme includes weekly department presentations from senior leadership, a career mentor, networking with executive leadership, volunteer opportunities and a team case study delivered to the leadership team. PHLY, headquartered in Bala Cynwyd, Pennsylvania, is a member of the[Tokio Marine Group](https://www.phly.com/aboutphly) and has been named a[Best Place to Work in Insurance since 2010](https://www.phly.com/aboutphly) , a Philadelphia Inquirer Top Workplace for 17 consecutive years, and a Forbes America’s Best Midsize Employer four times. The company also runs a post-graduation[Trainee Program](https://www.phly.com/careers/students) of 6 to 18 months in Underwriting, Risk Management or Marketing, with paid industry designations. PHLY’s Indeed rating is[3.7 out of 5 from 161 reviews](https://www.indeed.com/cmp/Philadelphia-Insurance-Companies/reviews) , and its intern-filtered themes include “Ability to meet personal goals,” “Feeling of personal appreciation” and “Time and location flexibility.”

Set a daily job notification on the board now, join the Talent Network, and consider contacting a PHLY Talent Acquisition Advisor directly, which the[students page](https://www.phly.com/careers/students) explicitly offers.

### Why You Must Apply the Week Applications Open


PHLY is a mid-size carrier with 2,100 employees and a small corporate intern class. The Summer Associates Program is a named, structured cohort, not a rotating door, and with 120 niche market specialties generating only a handful of intern seats, the class fills quickly once posted. PHLY publishes no deadline, which means the closing signal is the requisition disappearing from the board. The company also lists community involvement as a stated requirement, not a nice-to-have, so the application itself needs evidence that takes time to build. Do not wait until the posting appears to assemble your materials. Have a resume that shows a 3.0-plus GPA, real extracurricular involvement, customer-service experience and a stated interest in insurance ready to submit the day the requisition goes live. And use PHLY’s own recruiter access: the students page offers “Contact a PHLY Talent Acquisition Advisor,” which is an unusually direct pre-application channel.

## Which Philadelphia Insurance Companies Internship Programs Should You Target?


PHLY offers two structured entry points for early-career candidates, plus seven named career paths. Which one to target depends on whether you are still enrolled or about to graduate.


Program Focus Duration Key details


Summer Associates Program Department-specific work across Insurance Operations, Underwriting, Risk Management, Claims, Marketing, HR or Compliance 10 weeks (June–August) Paid hourly; team case study delivered to leadership; weekly senior-leadership presentations; career mentor; executive networking; volunteer opportunities


Trainee Program Post-graduation development in Underwriting, Risk Management or Marketing 6–18 months Classroom instruction, on-the-job training, mentoring, paid industry-recognised designations; launches a P&C insurance career


See all openings on the[PHLY students and new graduates page](https://www.phly.com/careers/students) . The Summer Associates Program is the entry point for current students; the Trainee Program is the equivalent for graduating seniors and recent graduates.


## What Are the Eligibility Requirements?


PHLY publishes a complete “Who We’re Looking For” list for the Summer Associates Program, which is unusually specific for a company of this size:


• **Class year:** rising junior or senior pursuing a bachelor’s degree.


• **GPA:** cumulative 3.0 or higher. PHLY states this explicitly, which is rare among employers of its size.


• **Interest:** “Interest in learning about the Insurance Industry” — not prior experience, not a risk-management major.


• **Extracurriculars:** “Involvement in community and extracurricular activities” — listed as a requirement, not a nice-to-have, consistent with PHLY’s Civic 50 recognition and paid volunteer time off.


• **Communication:** excellent written and verbal communication skills.


• **Customer service:** excellent customer-service skills.


• **Major:** not restricted. PHLY names paths from actuarial science to operations to underwriting but sets no major requirement.


• **Work authorization:** not published. PHLY states no visa or sponsorship policy for interns.


### Does PHLY Have a Hard GPA Cutoff?


Yes, 3.0. PHLY is one of the few employers in this category that publishes an explicit GPA floor, and it sits in the “Who We’re Looking For” list alongside class year and extracurricular involvement. It is a real screen. But the rest of the bar is genuinely accessible: no specific major, no technical-skill requirement, no prior insurance experience. The qualification is curiosity about insurance, a record of doing things outside class, and the ability to communicate. If your GPA is at or above 3.0 and you have a genuine community-involvement story, you clear the stated requirements for a company that an independent Harvard-affiliated study ranked in the American top 22 for early-career job quality.


## What Skills Does Philadelphia Insurance Companies Look For, and How Do You Build Them?


PHLY had zero intern requisitions live when this research was conducted, so there is no JD-sampled skill frequency to report. Instead, the skills below come from two sources: PHLY’s own published Summer Associates requirements on its students page, and dated first-hand intern reviews. PHLY names no software, no technical tool, no programming language and no certification for the internship. What it screens for is communication, customer service, community involvement, critical thinking about insurance work, and the ability to collaborate toward a capstone case study. That profile is genuinely different from a tech or finance employer, and a candidate who leads with Excel and Python is answering a question PHLY did not ask.

## What Is the Philadelphia Insurance Companies Application and Interview Process Like?


PHLY does not publish a step-by-step hiring process for the Summer Associates Program. The guidance below is constructed from the programme’s published structure and the available application channels:


1. **Set a daily job notification** at[phly-jobs.ttcportals.com](https://phly-jobs.ttcportals.com/search/jobs) . On any search-results page, use “Notify me of new jobs,” name the notification and set it to Daily. This is the single most useful action for a reader in autumn 2026.


2. **Join the Talent Network** for recruiter visibility. The board offers a sign-up at the bottom of every page.


3. **Contact a PHLY Talent Acquisition Advisor** with questions before applying. The[students page](https://www.phly.com/careers/students) explicitly offers this, and very few employers publish that kind of direct access.


4. **Apply through the external board** at phly-jobs.ttcportals.com when the Summer Associate requisition posts. Use the Business Unit and Location facets to filter, not the keyword search box (keyword filtering is client-side and does not discriminate).


5. **Prepare for a team case study question** in the interview. The programme’s capstone is “participation in a team case study which will be delivered to the leadership team,” so the interview will likely probe for teamwork under a deadline with an executive audience.


Because PHLY publishes no interview structure, timelines will vary by department. Prepare behavioural answers focused on customer-service situations, teamwork and community involvement, all of which appear in PHLY’s stated requirements. Our[HireVue question guide with a free AI mock tool](https://www.extern.com/post/hirevue-interview-questions-2025-free-ai-mock-tool) covers the same behavioural-question pressure and format.

## How Do You Stand Out at a Company That Publishes Its Own Screening Criteria?


Three moves, all executable before the requisition posts. First, clear the 3.0 GPA bar and have the transcript ready to prove it. Second, build real community involvement, not resume padding. PHLY lists “Involvement in community and extracurricular activities” as a stated requirement, not a tiebreaker, and the company sits on the Civic 50 list with paid volunteer time off. Third, say you want to learn insurance, in those exact words. The stated requirement is “Interest in learning about the Insurance Industry,” and the strongest way to demonstrate that is to know what PHLY actually does: 120 niche market specialties in property/casualty and professional liability, sold through agents and brokers, rated A++ by AM Best. Cite the Where You Work Matters badge back to them correctly: the study is outcome-based and independent (not a survey PHLY submitted to), and the CEO’s quote frames it as being about “our people and the culture they bring to life every day.” Knowing that shows you read past the logo.

## FAQ


### Can I still apply for a summer 2026 Philadelphia Insurance Companies internship?


No. The summer 2026 cohort has already started. The next open cycle is summer 2027. PHLY publishes no application-open date, but the programme runs June through August, so watch the board at phly-jobs.ttcportals.com through autumn and winter 2026 and apply the day the Summer Associate requisition appears.


### What GPA do I need for a PHLY internship?


A cumulative 3.0 or higher. PHLY states it explicitly in its Who We’re Looking For list, which is unusual. Most employers of this size publish no GPA figure at all.


### How much do PHLY interns get paid?


PHLY confirms the programme carries a “competitive hourly salary” but publishes no figure. No Summer Associate requisition was live to carry a pay range, and Indeed has no salary sample for the title at PHLY. The internship is confirmed paid hourly.


### Where are PHLY internships based?


The headquarters is at One Bala Plaza in Bala Cynwyd, Pennsylvania, just outside Philadelphia, and it is the company’s largest single location. Past interns have also reviewed from Timonium, Maryland, Garden City, New York, and Glen Allen, Virginia. A March 2025 intern confirmed a hybrid schedule. PHLY has offices in 22 states.


### What departments can I intern in at PHLY?


PHLY names seven early-career paths: Insurance Operations, Underwriting, Risk Management, Claims, Marketing, Human Resources and Compliance. Note that Marketing at PHLY means agency-facing distribution, qualifying leads and soliciting business through agents, wholesalers and brokers, not brand marketing.


### Is there a deadline for the PHLY Summer Associates Program?


None is published. PHLY states no application deadline on its careers pages, its student page, or any of its requisitions. If an aggregator shows a closing date on a PHLY posting, that is the aggregator’s own expiry, not PHLY’s.


### What happens after the PHLY internship?


PHLY does not publish a conversion rate. It does run a post-graduation Trainee Program of 6 to 18 months in Underwriting, Risk Management or Marketing, with classroom instruction, on-the-job training, mentoring and paid industry-recognised designations. The stronger signal is external: in the 2026 Where You Work Matters study, PHLY was one of just 22 employers to earn platinum in all three categories, including Early Career Jobs and Growth Jobs.


### Does PHLY sponsor visas for interns?


Not found. PHLY publishes no work-authorization or sponsorship policy on its careers pages or student page. The students page offers “Contact a PHLY Talent Acquisition Advisor,” which is the right place to ask.


PHLY’s Summer Associates Program has not posted for summer 2027 yet, and there is no deadline to watch for. Spend the runway building proof: a[remote Externship](https://www.extern.com/externships) turns “interested in insurance” into a finished project a fall 2026 application can point at.
